welcomeParagraphs: I’m a Poet and a Poetry and Creative Writing Teacher. Since 2009 my poems have been published in newspapers, literary journals, magazines and anthologies in Ireland, The UK, Austria, America and Australia and they’ve been broadcast on TV, radio and online podcasts in Ireland and America.

In 2016 I received the Arts Council of Ireland Emerging Writer Award and in 2017 my poem SEVEN SUGAR CUBES was voted Irish Poem of the Year at the Bord Gáis Energy Irish Book Awards. In 2019 Edna O’Brien DBE selected me for the UK Clarissa Luard Emerging Writer Award. I’ve also given public readings of my poems in several universities in America and at public events and festivals in Ireland and the UK.

When I’m not writing or teaching I’m fully immersed in motherhood and busy family life with my husband and our four children (aged 21, 18, 15 and 15). We live in the beautiful harbour town of Dungarvan, Co. Waterford in the southeast of Ireland (where I was born and raised).

paragraphs: Award-winning Irish Poet, Clodagh Beresford Dunne was born in Dublin in 1975 and raised in the harbour town of Dungarvan, Co. Waterford, in the southeast of Ireland. She grew up in a local newspaper family (‘The Dungarvan Observer’, a weekly broadsheet having been founded by her great-grandfather, James A. Lynch, in 1912). During her childhood, her grandfather P.J. Lynch was editor of the newspaper, and both of her parents worked alongside him. Her writing was first published in the ‘Dungarvan Observer’ when she was 8 years old.

She was educated in the Presentation Convent, Dungarvan and in Rockwell College Cashel and earned degrees in English and in Law from University College Galway (1995 and 1997 respectively). She apprenticed and practised as a qualified solicitor in Dublin from 1998 to 2005, receiving her parchment from the Law Society of Ireland in the Long Vacation of 2000. During her university and training years, she was an award-winning public speaker and debater (LAMDA Gold Medal recipient), was a finalist in the Irish Times Debating Competition and represented Ireland on two occasions at the World Universities Debating Championships, including at Princeton University.

Her poems have been published in outlets including The Irish Times, Poetry Magazine (Chicago), Poetry Ireland Review, The Stinging Fly, The Moth, Southword, The London Magazine, Poetry Salzburg Review, The Woven Tale Press (New York), The High Window, 14 Magazine, Magma, and Cordite (Australia). The Arts Council of Ireland has awarded her its Emerging Writer Award, its Agility Award and a Travel and Training Award. She was the winner of The Irish Book Awards Irish Poem of the Year Award for ‘Seven Sugar Cubes’ and, at the request of Edna O’Brien DBE, she received the 2019 Arts Council of England’s Clarissa Luard Emerging Writer Award.

Clodagh has given readings and lectures on her work in Ireland, the UK and in several universities in the USA; she served as adjudicator for the Listowel Writers’ Week National Pigott Poetry Prize, and she has taught Creative Writing and Poetry to school students, university students, and adults for over 16 years.

testimonials.quote: Here is a brilliant writer. She is a young poet with an old soul. By that I mean she has ancient wisdom and thrust but also a modern, searching, brave sensibility. Clodagh Beresford Dunne is a writer in love with language.
testimonials.author: Edna O’Brien DBE
testimonials.role: Recipient of the David Cohen Prize for Literature

newsEvents.title: Full Day Poetry Workshop: “Titles & Opening Lines”
newsEvents.location: Colligan Falls, Dungarvan, Co. Waterford (X35 YC66)
newsEvents.summary: An intensive intermediate/advanced full-day poetry workshop (9:30 am – 5:00 pm) examining the titles and opening lines of 20 contemporary poems, workshopping 2 poems per participant, plus 200-word written follow-up feedback. Group strictly capped at 7 participants (€150 pp, lunch included).

newsEvents.title: Leaving Certificate English — Fortnightly Friday Sessions
newsEvents.summary: Fortnightly two-hour sessions covering Paper 1 (The Essay: ideas, structure, technique) and Paper 2 (Prescribed & Unseen Poetry: analysis, personal response, quote recall, vocabulary expansion). Higher & Ordinary Levels, full notes provided (€50 pp).

newsEvents.title: ‘Cordgrass’ Published in Magma Poetry (Grassroots Issue)
newsEvents.summary: Clodagh’s spatial poem ‘Cordgrass’, connecting the landscape of Scarborough Marsh with Irish heritage and St. Brigid’s crosses, was published in the Grassroots Issue of Magma Magazine.

newsEvents.title: Poem of the Week in The Irish Times: ‘At the King’s Coronation...’
newsEvents.summary: ‘At the King’s Coronation the talk is of the Weight of his Once-Off Crown’, reflecting on her late father’s time as a Buckingham Palace Guard, featured as Poem of the Week in The Irish Times.
